raw.transcript: First, restart your router and modem by unplugging them, waiting about 15 seconds, then plugging them back in and giving them a minute to settle. Next, on your computer or phone, turn Wi‑Fi off, wait a few seconds, then turn it back on and reconnect to your network. Third, move closer to the router, and if you can, reduce interference by keeping it away from thick walls, metal objects, and crowded electronics. Fourth, “forget” the network in your device’s Wi‑Fi settings and then rejoin it by entering the password again. Fifth, update your network drivers or your device’s operating system, and if your router has a firmware update available, apply that too. Sixth, if it still drops, try a different channel or band, like switching between 2.4 gigahertz and 5 gigahertz, and if problems continue after that, contact your internet provider, because there may be a line or service issue outside your home.
